facts.statement: Miadanasuchus was an extinct genus of peirosaurid notosuchian that lived in Madagascar during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Miadanasuchus is an extinct genus of peirosaurid notosuchian which lived in Madagascar during the late Cretaceous period.

facts.statement: The species was first described as Trematochampsa oblita by Éric Buffetaut and Philippe Taquet in 1979 based on fossils from the Maevarano Formation.
facts.quote: The species was first described as Trematochampsa oblita by Éric Buffetaut and Philippe Taquet in 1979, based on fossils found in an unknown member of the Maastrichtian aged Maevarano Formation.

facts.statement: Additional material of the species was discovered since 1993 in the Miadana Hills near the village of Berivotra.
facts.quote: Since 1993, subsequent discoveries in the Miadana Hills, near the village of Berivotra, brought more material of the species to scientific attention.

facts.statement: Miadanasuchus had teeth that were irregularly spaced and variable in height.
facts.quote: Its teeth were irregularly spaced and variable in height.

facts.statement: Miadanasuchus is estimated to have been 3 meters in length.
facts.quote: Miadanasuchus is estimated to have been 3 m in length.

facts.statement: Fossils found in the Ankazomihaboka Formation potentially extend the species' temporal range back to the Coniacian.
facts.quote: additional material referred to Miadanasuchus (teeth, vertebrae, and a single osteoderm) has also been found in the Ankazomihaboka Formation, potentially extending the species' temporal range as far back as the Coniacian.

facts.statement: Miadanasuchus belongs to the parent group Peirosauridae.
Miadanasuchus is classified in the family Peirosauridae.
Miadanasuchus is classified in the class Reptilia.
Miadanasuchus lived during the Maastrichtian stage, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

rejected.statement: In 2009, Simons and Buckley erected the new genus Miadanasuchus because there was an absence of synapomorphies between Trematochampsa taqueti and Miadanasuchus oblita compared to other trematochampsids.
rejected.quote: In 2009, Erin L. Rasmusson Simons and Gregory A. Buckley determined that since there was "an absence of synapomorphies between Trematochampsa taqueti and Miadanasuchus oblita to the exception of all other trematochampsids", it warranted the erection of a new genus.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'there was an absence of synapomorphies between Trematochampsa'
